meta.title: L'agent reformule — le coordinateur → son sous-agent
meta.source: claude-code (le prompt exact envoyé au sous-agent, copié du terminal)
meta.note: Ce que le coordinateur a écrit à son sous-agent après mes deux lignes « could the editor be part of the rust thing?… » et « can you start the rust editor in a worktree? ». La réponse du sous-agent n'a pas été gardée.

turns.text:
Work ONLY in <scratchpad>/wt-editor (a git worktree of the repo with today's uncommitted state copied in; `target/` is a symlink to the main cargo cache; do NOT git commit; do NOT touch ~/workspace/open-miami — another agent works there on src/props.rs; your changes will be 3-way merged later, so keep your edits to lib.rs SMALL and localized (new code goes in NEW files) and do not reformat/reorder unrelated code). Do NOT run `make check-e2e` (policy: slow; the coordinator runs it before commits) — your gate is `make verify` + `make build-wasm` + targeted headless screenshots.

  READ FIRST: CLAUDE.md, docs/SCENARIO_FORMAT.md, docs/PROPS_FORMAT.md, src/lib.rs (the ?viz toolbox: tabs, `draw_viz_levels` fallback map, `viz_button`, `draw_viz_props` and its PIXEL/GRID/SAVE controls + the `vizSaveProps` extern bridge, `draw_viz_sprites`, mouse/click plumbing, `url_flag/url_param`), src/scenario.rs (`FloorDef` and friends — static refs), src/levels.rs, src/levels_data.rs (GENERATED by tools/gen_levels.py from levels/*.json), tools/gen_levels.py, src/level.rs + src/render.rs (how the floor/walls are drawn in-game, `render_walls`), src/props.rs (`PROP_NAMES`, `PROP_LAYERS`, `draw_prop`, `draw_prop_ex`, `prop_px`, `PropDrawOpts`, `snap_size`), src/graphics.rs (transforms, pixel_begin/pixel_end, draw_text), src/input.rs (keys, mouse, `any_pressed`), src/camera.rs, index.html (`vizInspect`, `vizSaveProps` bridge + toast), serve.py (PUT API + token), tools/levels.html (the current HTML editor — the thing phase 1 starts replacing; keep it working for the scenario/steps side for now).

  GOAL — Phase 1 of a NATIVE (Rust/wasm, drawn with the game's own renderer) level editor + PROP PLACEMENT end to end:
  1. FORMAT: floors gain `"props": [ { "kind": "rack_closed", "x": 120, "y": 340, "rot": 0, "size": 100 } ]` (rot in degrees, multiples of 90 preferred but any allowed; size in world units, default 100 = the prop's design box). Extend tools/gen_levels.py (validate kind ∈ PROP_NAMES snake_case ids — read them from src/props.rs like gen_props.py does — and emit `props: &[PropPlacement]` into `FloorDef`), src/scenario.rs `FloorDef` (+ `PropPlacement` struct), regenerate src/levels_data.rs (`make gen-levels`), update docs/SCENARIO_FORMAT.md, and the HTML editor's format module (`tools/levels-editor-format.js`: preserve/round-trip an unknown-to-it `props` array untouched — do NOT build prop editing in the HTML editor). Add a few placed props to 2–3 floors (e.g. floor 1 reception: racks/desk; floor 11: racks around the ring) as demo content.
  2. GAME RENDER: draw placed props in-game UNDER actors and OVER the floor tiles (after `level.render`, before walls or after? props are floor furniture: draw after floor tiles, before walls' shadow? — simplest: after `render_walls`, before `render_entities`), using `props::draw_prop_ex(g, kind, center, size, t, prop_px(kind), &default opts)` with the prop's own saved pixel grid, rotated by `rot`; props are decoration only (no collision) in phase 1 — say so in the docs. Respect the `?pixel=N` world group if present (props are inside it anyway).
  3. NATIVE EDITOR (new files `src/editor.rs` + maybe `src/editor_ui.rs`): replaces the LEVELS tab content (the iframe stays available behind a "SCENARIO (web)" button that calls `viz_inspect("levels")` for the steps/dialogue side; the tab itself now shows the native spatial editor). Features: floor picker (◀ ▶ + name), the floor rendered with the REAL renderer (floor tiles, walls, elevators via render_comms's elevator drawing if reusable, zones/rooms outlines with labels, spawns as coloured diamonds by type, pickups, entry/exits, and PROPS animated live at their pixel grid), camera pan (drag with middle/space or right-drag) + wheel zoom (add a wheel event in input.rs if none) + FIT; grid + snap (10 units default, toggle); tools: SELECT/MOVE (drag; resize handles for rects), WALL, ROOM, ZONE, SPAWN (type cycle), PICKUP (weapon cycle), ENTRY, EXIT, PROP (a palette: family pages DATACENTER/… showing prop thumbnails via draw_prop, click to pick, click on map to place; R rotates 90°, [ ] resize, arrow keys nudge, Del deletes); an editable in-memory `EditableFloor` (owned Vecs; `from(&FloorDef)`, `to_json()` hand-written serializer producing the documented key order and round-tripping the scenario steps/exits/etc. verbatim — implement a tiny JSON writer; no serde, no crates); undo/redo (snapshot stack, 100); a small text-field widget for ids/labels (click to focus, type, Enter/Esc; use input keys) — keep it minimal (walls need none; zones/rooms/exits ids/labels do); a properties strip for the selection; validation line (ids unique, exits' `to` valid, refs used by scenario exist — reuse rules from the doc); SAVE → wasm→JS extern `vizSaveLevel(file, json)` (add to index.html mirroring `vizSaveProps`, PUT /levels/<file>.json with the same token flow, toast with "now run: make gen-levels"). Keep `?viz`'s other tabs untouched. Keyboard shortcuts listed on-screen.
  4. Keep the fallback wasm LEVELS map (draw_viz_levels) as the FIT/overview if convenient or remove it — your call; don't leave dead code.

  CONSTRAINTS: no new deps; opcode tables untouched (no new opcodes needed); CLAUDE.md updated (?viz LEVELS = native editor + SCENARIO (web) button; props in floors; format); localized lib.rs edits (dispatch + a few fields), all real code in src/editor*.rs; unit tests for the JSON writer round-trip (parse the generated JSON back with a tiny test parser or compare against gen_levels.py: run `python3 tools/gen_levels.py --check` after writing a floor via the editor's serializer to prove it's accepted) and for EditableFloor edits/undo.

  VERIFY: `make verify` green (fmt, host+wasm clippy, tests, build, wasm, check-levels/props). `make build-wasm`; serve `python3 serve.py 8100` (port 8100 only, from the worktree root); headless Playwright (cd tests/e2e; chromium args --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader; LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(find "$PWD/tests/e2e/playwright-deps/libs" -name '*.so*' -printf '%h\n'|sort -u|paste -sd:)"; clicks/keys HELD 150 ms). Screenshots to shots/editor_native_*.png (in the worktree's shots/, create it): the LEVELS tab with floor 11 rendered natively incl. placed props; the prop palette open; a prop being placed/rotated; a wall drawn + zone with label; the SAVE toast; and `?floor=1` gameplay showing the placed props under the action. Zero console errors. Report: format change, generator, in-game render, the editor's architecture (files, widget set, EditableFloor + JSON writer), keyboard map, screenshots, caveats, and the exact lib.rs regions you touched. Ping when done; stop the 8100 server.
